title: Triage runbook pocket notes — Sofia Chen
summary: Quick-pocket triage runbook and day-to-day notes for investigating dashboard anomalies and customer-reported UI/metric inconsistencies.
body:
Purpose: scratchpad for quick repro steps, fast mitigations, and follow-ups while I’m on shift. Not a canonical runbook — copy to Confluence when polished.

How I use this: keep short reproducible commands, things I tried and why, and a minimal timeline so follow-up owners can pick up. Include links to tickets and short decisions.

Common mental model: most reporting errors come from 1) frontend telemetry mismatch, 2) ETL job lag (metrics pipeline), 3) cache mismatch between CDN and origin, 4) serving-runtime metric rollups delayed. Prioritize by customer impact + likelihood.

Quick triage flow (2-minute checklist):
- Confirm customer still sees the issue (ask for screenshot + exact time).
- Check alert rules: is there a firing alert? which rule?
- Open dashboard time window to problem time + 10m either side. Set timezone to user tz.
- Look at ingestion lag metric (metrics.pipeline.*.lag). If >30s, start here.
- If ingestion looks fine, check service-level traces for 5xx / long tails.
- If frontend-only, inspect Sentry/session logs for JS errors and feature flags.

Note: default time window I use for investigation is now() - 1h to now() unless customer gives exact timestamp.

quick_hits: kubectl -n obs get pods -l app=metric-ingestor -o wide
psql -h analytics-read.prod -c "select max(processed_at) from metrics_ingest where pipeline='dashboard';"
follow_ups: @Luca - need ETL job logs (pipeline: dashboard) for 2026-03-09 02:00-03:00 UTC (ticket JIRA-5987).
@Priya - can you validate the fix for PR GH-PR-1342 on staging? low-risk toggle to roll back if needed.
Notify Customer Success (cs-team@redwood.ai) with summary and ETA before EOD if root cause confirmed.
If ingestion backfill needed, coordinate a maintenance window with infra and notify SLAs.
open_questions: Why did only dashboards with >10 series show the discrepancy? hypothesis: aggregation sharding change in last deploy.
Is there a delayed write to metrics.store between 02:10 and 02:20? need exact shard mapping.
Do front-end cached tiles depend on an edge TTL that could have been mis-set during deploy?
log_entries: 2026-03-11 08:42 - started triage after CS ping (customer: AcmeCorp). They reported missing spikes between 02:05-02:20 UTC.
2026-03-11 08:47 - checked alerting rules; none fired. Ingestion lag metric showed transient spike at 02:12 (~46s).
2026-03-11 09:02 - pulled ingestor pod logs; saw occasional timeout to clickhouse shard-3 around 02:11. Logged snippet to JIRA-5987.
2026-03-11 09:25 - triggered lightweight backfill (safe-window) for 02:00-02:30 on analytics-read; queued. Notified CS that we’re backfilling and monitoring.
2026-03-11 10:05 - backfill progress: 40% processed, no errors. Customer acknowledged receipt of update.
notes_for_handover: If you pick this up: start with the backfill status (Jenkins job id in JIRA), then check ClickHouse shard health. If backfill succeeds, verify affected dashboards and close JIRA with postmortem notes. Assign rollback to infra if replication lag persists.
micro_runbook_steps: 2) Run ingestion lag query (psql snippet above).
3) Check ingestor pod logs for timeouts (kubectl logs -p).
4) If timeout: restart single ingestor pod with grace period, watch latency. Use rolling restart only if multiple pods show same error.
5) Start safe backfill for narrow window if data missing; document job id.
final_reminder: This is a working note — move confirmed mitigation steps and postmortem into Confluence and tag stakeholders. Keep this doc ephemeral; delete or archive after closure.
